title: Sisporta — Resilient Data Synchronization Pipeline
subtitle: Asynchronous Integration Pipeline, Python ETL Agent & Delete-by-Absence Strategy
summary: Decoupled and resilient data pipeline syncing an untouchable legacy SQL Server ERP to a modern Laravel platform via a Python ETL agent, asynchronous Laravel Horizon queues, and delete-by-absence mirror logic.
overview: The Sisporta project was born from the classic engineering challenge of modernizing enterprise quotation workflows without touching an untouchable legacy SQL Server ERP database. The solution was an asynchronous, resilient data pipeline: an external Python ETL agent reads active records from SQL Server and batches JSON payloads to a modern Laravel API. Ingestion is fully decoupled using Laravel Horizon queues, where background workers process updates and execute an automated 'delete-by-absence' cleanup job, guaranteeing an exact, clean mirror of ERP products and dealers without leaving orphaned or stale records.
responsibilities: Architecture Design: Conceptualized the asynchronous integration architecture ensuring high throughput and complete decoupling from legacy ERP.
Python ETL Agent: Developed the automated extraction script collecting and formatting commercial entities from SQL Server.
Laravel Application & Queues: Implemented ingestion API endpoints and distributed job handling with Laravel Horizon.
CI/CD Pipeline: Automated testing suites and continuous deployment pipelines using Bitbucket Pipelines.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Synchronizing enterprise datasets without write access to database schemas, views, or triggers in the legacy SQL Server ERP.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Built an external Python ETL runner conducting non-blocking reads paired with a full-refresh 'delete-by-absence' mirroring routine.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Guaranteeing fault tolerance and zero data loss during high-volume batch sync cycles.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Leveraged Laravel Horizon asynchronous queues with automated retry backoffs and isolated dead-letter handling.
